trait: Lactase persistence (digesting milk sugar as an adult)
reading: No copy of -13910T, the European lactase persistence allele. In people of European descent lactase activity then usually falls after childhood. This alone does not prove lactose intolerance: other persistence alleles exist, the African ones of the rows below among them, and this table does not hold every one.
note: Lactase persistence is dominant: one copy of a persistence allele is usually enough. -13910T explains it in Europeans; in Africa and the Middle East other alleles do (rows -14010, -13915, -13907 and -14009). These rows hold the main known persistence alleles, not every one, so a genotype with none of them does not prove lactase non-persistence.

trait: Red hair and fair skin (MC1R R151C)
reading: No R151C.
note: Red hair usually needs a red-hair MC1R variant on both copies of the gene: the same one twice, or two different ones (rows rs1805007, rs1805008, rs1805009). One copy at two of these rows can mean one on each copy; the phase is not known here. In a study of red-haired British families and unrelated people (Flanagan 2000), red hair was usually recessive and the effect grew with the number of variant copies. These are findings of the people studied, not rules: MC1R variants are not always enough for red hair (in a study of 25 red-haired and 62 other twins, some twin pairs with the same MC1R alleles differed in hair colour), and some red-haired people carry only one variant copy, or other MC1R variants than these three.

reading: e3/e3, the most common pair: the reference group for Alzheimer's risk.
note: Odds ratios of Alzheimer's disease against e3/e3 from a meta-analysis of clinic and autopsy studies of people of European descent (Farrer 1997), adjusted for age: odds ratios of those case-control studies, not a lifetime risk. Step 25's Alzheimer's score (PGS000334) includes the same two sites; docs/42-traits.md says why step 06 does not list APOE.
